newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi shares slump, fail to revive.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi shares slump, fail to revive.

text.p: Trade at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) slumped to a fresh low since May and failed to pick up after calls for constitutional reform upset market nerves on Monday, brokers officials said.
Turnover was posted at 93.2 million shillings for the week ending Friday compared to 170.9 million shillings last week.
A total of 1.3 million shares were traded this week compared to 38.8 million shares traded last week.
The NSE 20-share index eased 0.92 points in the same period to close at 3502.76. But on Friday, it eased 3.67 points from Thursday's levels.

Brokers said activity at the Nairobi bourse, supported by heavy foreign demand, had cooled down after many foreign funds opted to withhold fresh investments despite a return to normality after violent protests on Monday.

Nine people were killed in Kenya on Monday during the most violent clashes between police and protesters since a campaign in July 1990 that helped persuade President Daniel arap Moi to allow multi-party politics.
"They're apprehensive because of the unstable political situation. This week as a whole has been one of the poorest in the market," a senior broker told Reuters.

Brokers said that foreign investors drawn to Kenya because of attractive yields made on interest rate differentials and a stable currency were selling their bonds after the shilling took a major beating this week.

"It will be disastrous if the shilling depreciates further. Foreigners are not coming in and they feel its better to offload and are looking elsewhere," a senior executive at a top brokerage firm told Reuters.

Commercial bank dealers posted rates in the 59-61 range and maintained spreads as wide as three shillings. The shilling last touched the 60 range and threatened further losses versus the dollar in October 1993.
Bank dealers said Thursday's move from 56.30 to a close as low as 59.30 against the dollar had sent waves of panic in the market -- which they thought was an overreaction.
Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 101 from 107 while Barclays Bank was unchanged at 111. National Bank of Kenya closed at 15.50 from 16.
Firestone East Africa was unchanged at 29.25 while Kenya Breweries held steady at 57.
Kenya Airways closed at 8.0 unchanged while Uchumi Supermarket eased to 37.50 from 39.
Rea Vipingo Plantations eased to 10.05 from 10.50 while Kapchorua was steady at 105.
